q1.question: What is JoinOrigin?
q1.answer: Origin is the space you start around a goal. You bring the idea, gather the people and resources it needs, and move it forward together. JoinOrigin is the brand and the network behind it. Instead of five separate tools, your relationships live in one place, so nothing gets lost between them.

q5.question: How do I join?

hero.title: Everything an Origin needs, in one calm workspace
hero.lead: Origin is built around eight core objects: profiles, ideas, Origins, communication, feed, projects, companies, and opportunities. Start an Origin for anything you want to happen — a startup, a small business, a project — and find the co-founders, partners, clients, and supporters who'll move it forward with you.

profiles.body: A profile works like a living resume: it carries your experience, skills, and ideas — plus your reputation and relationships — across every Origin and project you join.

ideas.body: Every Origin starts with an idea. Post an idea page for anything — a small business, an AI startup, a book club, a 10k run — and the people who want to build it find you.

communities.body: The space you start around a goal — a startup, a small business, a book club, or any idea. Every Origin gathers the people who share it and comes with its own room where the work moves forward.

communication.body: Every Origin comes with a Matrix room: real-time chat, direct messages, and group discussions over the open Matrix protocol, end-to-end encrypted by default.

feed.body: The feed shows posts, updates, and opportunities from the people and Origins you follow. It is a calm stream of what matters in your network, not an engagement machine.

projects.body: Collaborative efforts where the people in your Origin work together and turn conversations into outcomes.

companies.body: Ventures formed from Origins inside the network, with team management and opportunity sharing built in.

opportunities.body: Jobs, partnerships, clients, and investments discovered through the social graph — your Origin surfaces the right opportunities at the right time.

features.sectionComparison: Why Origin instead of ten tools
features.comparisonIntro: Most platforms solve only one part of collaboration. Origin combines them around the social graph — the relationships between members — so nothing gets lost between tools.

slack.gap: but is built for a single workspace — it does not carry profiles, Origins, projects, and opportunities across the people you already know.

discord.gap: but is not organized around profiles, Origins, projects, and opportunities on a shared social graph.

whatsapp.gap: but is a private chat app — it does not give Origins durable profiles, projects, and discovery on a shared social graph.

linkedin.gap: but does not power the Origins, chat, and projects that turn connections into collaboration.

meetup.gap: but is built around one-time RSVPs — it does not carry the Origin, projects, and relationships that grow after the event.

eventbrite.gap: but manages events, not Origins — it does not give your group a lasting home with profiles, projects, and opportunities.

notion.gap: but is a document tool — it does not connect the people behind the pages into an Origin that works together.

asana.gap: but is built for tasks, not relationships — it does not surface the people and Origins that make projects happen.

patreon.gap: but is built around subscriptions — it does not give your members profiles, projects, and Origins on a shared social graph.

facebook.gap: but is built around an advertising feed — it does not give Origins a calm workspace with profiles, projects, and opportunities.

phase2.body: Projects, shared workspaces, and tools that turn conversations into joint work. Success metric: Origins shipping outcomes together.

phase3.body: Companies and ventures formed by members, with team management and governance. Success metric: companies founded inside the network.

q1.question: How is JoinOrigin different from Discord?
q1.answer: Discord is a chat app. Origin is a social collaboration network — profiles, ideas, Origins, chat, feed, projects, and companies all live on one social graph.

q2.question: Is JoinOrigin open source?
q2.answer: The code is open under AGPL-3.0, and communication runs on the open Matrix protocol. Your data stays portable.

q3.question: What is the social graph?
q3.answer: The social graph is the web of relationships between members. Origin is organized around it, so every profile, Origin, and project connects through people.

q4.question: When will projects and companies launch?
q4.answer: They develop naturally. As people post ideas, visions, and work, they find the people who want to build with them — and projects and companies grow out of those connections instead of waiting for a launch date.

peopleFirst.body: Members are people, not profiles in a database. Every design decision protects the relationships that make an Origin worth starting.

communitiesDriveGrowth.body: Origins are the center of engagement. When an Origin thrives, the people in it find each other, share what they need, and build together.

collaborationCreatesValue.body: Collaboration is how conversations become projects and projects become companies. Origin is built so collaboration has somewhere to go.

q1.question: What Origins can I join?
q1.answer: Anyone can start or join an Origin around any idea — a small business, an AI startup, helping the homeless, a 10k run, a political movement, a pee-wee league. If it matters to you, it has a place on Origin.

q2.question: Can I start my own Origin?
q2.answer: Yes. Every member can create an Origin around any idea and invite the people they want to build with — whether it is a business, a book club, or a run club.

q3.question: Is my data mine?
q3.answer: Yes. You own your identity and your data. Your data is portable and your network graph persists on the open Matrix protocol.

q4.question: How do I find my people?
q4.answer: Browse Origins by interest, industry, or goal — from small businesses and book clubs to AI startups and run clubs — then join the ones that match what you want to build. Or start your own for any idea.

q5.question: Can I join anonymously or by name?
q5.answer: You choose. You can participate with a named account or stay anonymous, and Origins, rooms, and idea pages can be open to everyone or gated by organizers. These options roll out over time.

hero.title: JoinOrigin docs
hero.lead: Origin is the product: a social collaboration network and community OS. JoinOrigin is the brand and the network behind it. These docs explain the core objects, the roadmap, and the architecture.

profiles.body: Profiles are the portable identity of every member — like a living resume. They carry experience, skills, ideas, reputation, and relationships across every community and project, so who you are travels with you.

communities.body: Origins are the space you start around a goal — a group of people who share interests, industries, goals, and opportunities around any idea. They are the center of engagement on Origin and the way members find each other.

ideas.body: Every idea gets a home. Post an idea page for anything — a small business, an AI startup, helping the homeless, a 10k run, a book club, a pee-wee league — and find the people who want to build it with you.

communication.body: Communication happens in a Matrix room — real-time chat, direct messages, and group discussions. It runs on the open Matrix protocol, so conversations are portable and can be end-to-end encrypted.

feed.body: Posts, updates, and opportunities from the people and communities you follow — a calm stream of what matters in your network.

projects.body: Projects are collaborative efforts where members work together toward a shared outcome. They connect the social graph to real work inside and across communities.

companies.body: Companies are ventures formed by members of the network. They bring team management and opportunity sharing into the same workspace where the relationships live.

opportunities.body: Opportunities are jobs, partnerships, and investments surfaced through the social graph. The network matches the right opportunity to the right person at the right time.

phase1.body: Profiles, Origins, chat, and the social graph. Success metric: members forming durable Origins.

phase2.body: Projects, shared workspaces, and tools that turn conversations into joint work. Success metric: Origins shipping outcomes together.

phase3.body: Companies and ventures formed by members, with team management and governance. Success metric: companies founded inside the network.

phase4.body: AI workers that help Origins coordinate, summarize, and match opportunities. Success metric: members collaborating with AI as equals.

phase5.body: Open standards and portability so the network connects across platforms. Success metric: a portable, interoperable social graph.

docs.architectureParagraph1: The social graph is the product: every object hangs off the network of people and their relationships. Communication uses the open Matrix protocol (decentralized, E2EE), and your network graph and connections persist forever, so your relationships stay portable.
docs.architectureParagraph2: Origin is built with React, TypeScript, and Next.js on the web, and NestJS, PostgreSQL, Redis, and Docker in the backend. What stays open is the protocol (Matrix), your data, and the source code under AGPL-3.0.

q1.question: What is JoinOrigin built on?
q1.answer: React, TypeScript, and Next.js on the web; NestJS, PostgreSQL, Redis, and Docker in the backend. Communication runs on the open Matrix protocol.

q2.question: What is Matrix?
q2.answer: Matrix is an open, decentralized communication protocol with end-to-end encryption. Origin runs on it, so conversations — and the network graph behind them — are portable and persist forever.

q4.question: What is live now?
q4.answer: The Origin Foundation (Phase 1) is live: profiles, Origins, chat, and the social graph are already in use by 2,400+ builders.

hero.lead: When you get started we collect your name and email address through the signup form (POST /api/leads). That is the only personal information we ask for.

collect.analyticsBody: We run config-driven analytics (self-hosted Plausible by default) to understand aggregate usage of the site. A consent banner is planned for a later sprint.
collect.technicalDataBody: Standard server logs and browser metadata that help us keep the site reliable.

privacy.useBody: We use the information we collect to operate the site, manage your account and communities, and improve the product. We do not sell your personal information.
privacy.identityBody: You choose how you show up on Origin. You can participate with a named account or stay anonymous, and communities, chats, and idea pages can be open to everyone or gated by their organizers. glossary.title: Community OS Glossary
glossary.intro: The essential vocabulary of Origin — clear definitions for the terms organizers, moderators, and founders use every day.
glossary.whyBody: Building anything together has its own language, and the terms are often used loosely. An Origin glossary gives organizers, moderators, and founders shared definitions they can rely on — from the classic concepts like moderation and onboarding to newer ideas like engagement loops and hybrid events.
glossary.termsIntro: Here are the core terms every organizer, moderator, and founder uses — each one is defined in practice across the Community Building guides:
glossary.goDeeperItem1: Work through the <1>Community Building guides</1> — the step-by-step how-tos behind every term.
glossary.goDeeperItem2: See the concepts in practice: <1>New York City</1> and <2>Berlin</2> city pages.

community.name: Origin
community.definition: The space you start around a goal. An Origin gathers the people and resources needed to make something happen — a small business, an AI startup, a book club, or a 10k run. On Origin, every Origin comes with a room where members find each other and build together.

community-manager.name: Community manager
community-manager.definition: The person who keeps an Origin welcoming, active, and on-mission — welcoming new members, sparking conversation, and coordinating work. On Origin, the member who starts an Origin owns and moderates its room.

community-os.name: Community OS
community-os.definition: A platform that brings profiles, Origins, chat, projects, and opportunities into one organized workspace. Origin is the community OS behind JoinOrigin — the space where ideas, people, and resources move forward together.

moderation.name: Moderation
moderation.definition: The practice of keeping an Origin safe and on-topic through clear guidelines and consistent, fair enforcement. Good moderation protects the relationships that make an Origin worth joining.

onboarding.name: Onboarding
onboarding.definition: The process of welcoming new members and helping them take a first meaningful action — introducing themselves, joining a conversation, or starting a project. Strong onboarding turns new members into active ones.

activation.name: Activation
activation.definition: The moment a new member takes the action that makes them part of an Origin — their first post, first proposal, or first contribution. Activation is the step between joining and contributing.

engagement-loop.name: Engagement loop
engagement-loop.definition: The repeating cycle that moves an Origin forward: someone posts a need or an offer, others respond, and the work creates more reasons to return. Healthy loops are the heartbeat of an active Origin.

hybrid-events.name: Hybrid events
hybrid-events.definition: Events that blend in-person and online participation, so members in different places can join the same gathering. Hybrid formats help communities stay connected between meetups.

co-founder.name: Co-founder
co-founder.definition: A person who builds a project or company with you and shares the founding journey. On Origin, co-founders are often found through your Origin — people who answer a need or offer, join the work, and decide to build together.
